partners.mechanism_chain: GUSB (HGNC:4721) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal degradation of glycosaminoglycans (GO:0030146); Lysosomal degradation of glycosaminoglycans (GO:0030146) —DECREASES→ Accumulated GAGs (CHEBI:17786); Accumulated GAGs (CHEBI:17786) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatosplenomegaly (HP:0001652); Accumulated GAGs (CHEBI:17786) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000705); Accumulated GAGs (CHEBI:17786) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004305); Accumulated GAGs (CHEBI:17786) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001916); HBB (HGNC:4827) —DISRUPTS→ Heme biosynthesis and hemoglobin assembly (GO:0005837); Heme biosynthesis and hemoglobin assembly (GO:0005837) —DECREASES→ Anemia (HP:0001878); Heme biosynthesis and hemoglobin assembly (GO:0005837) —DISRUPTS→ Unstable alpha-globin chains (None); Unstable alpha-globin chains (None) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatosplenomegaly (HP:0001652); Unstable alpha-globin chains (None) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000705); Unstable alpha-globin chains (None) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004305); Unstable alpha-globin chains (None) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001916). Mutations in GUSB lead to impaired lysosomal degradation of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs), causing their accumulation and subsequent cellular dysfunction, manifesting as hepatosplenomegaly, skeletal abnormalities, short stature, and facial dysmorphism in MPS VII. In dominant beta-thalassemia, mutations in HBB lead to unstable or reduced production of beta-globin chains, resulting in ineffective erythropoiesis, anemia, and potentially accumulation of unstable alpha-globin chains, which can also contribute to cellular stress and affect downstream processes leading to overlapping phenotypes. The convergence is on cellular stress and downstream phenotypic effects caused by the accumulation of undegraded GAGs or aberrant globin chains.
